t: A sacred kingship in the hills east of Lake Tanganyika, whose dynasty tradition traces to Ntare Rushatsi around 1680.
Ntare IV Rugamba roughly doubled its territory in the early 19th century, giving Burundi borders close to today’s.
It survived German and Belgian rule to become independent in 1962, but army officer Michel Micombero abolished it in 1966.
dyk: The mountain gorilla’s species, Gorilla beringei, is named after Robert von Beringe, the German officer who shot two of the apes in 1902 and in 1903 led the campaign that forced Mwezi IV Gisabo to submit.
ev: Ntare Rushatsi founds the royal dynasty, according to tradition
Burundi and Rwanda partition the Kingdom of Bugesera
Mwezi IV Gisabo’s warriors repel the slave-trading forces of Rumaliza
Mwezi IV submits to German rule in the Treaty of Kiganda
Belgian troops occupy Burundi during the First World War
UPRONA wins the elections; its leader, Prince Louis Rwagasore, is assassinated
Burundi becomes independent as a constitutional monarchy under Mwambutsa IV
Michel Micombero deposes Ntare V and proclaims a republic

f.capital: Royal residences in the central highlands, notably Muramvya; Bujumbura after 1962
